records.first-paragraph:
If any of these deprecated features is a cause for concern for you, please
email the
[curl-library mailing list](https://lists.haxx.se/listinfo/curl-library)
as soon as possible and explain to us why this is a problem for you and
how your use case cannot be satisfied properly using a workaround.
records.section: Items to be removed from future curl releases
records.title: Items to be removed from future curl releases

records.first-paragraph:
The NTLM authentication method has weak security and is rarely used these
days. It has been deprecated by Microsoft and does not work over HTTP/2 or
HTTP/3.
records.heading: drop NTLM support

scheduled.sentence: NTLM support gets removed in September 2026

records.section: Items to be removed from future curl releases
records.title: drop NTLM support

records.first-paragraph:
Since the dawn of time, curl bundles code for a few crypto and hash algorithms
in order to enable functionality for builds without TLS libraries. This list
includes MD4, MD5, SHA256, SHA256_512 and perhaps something more.
records.heading: Local crypto implementations

scheduled.sentence: Local crypto gets removed in October 2026.

records.section: Items to be removed from future curl releases
records.title: Local crypto implementations

records.first-paragraph:
This protocol feature has been deprecated in specifications, by major browsers,
and in server implementations. It was never supported by the curl command line
tool, only by libcurl.
records.heading: HTTP/2 Server Push

scheduled.sentence: HTTP/2 Server Push gets removed in March 2027.

records.section: Items to be removed from future curl releases
records.title: HTTP/2 Server Push

records.first-paragraph:
The Common Name, (`CN`) field is deprecated since RFC 2818. It was downgraded
to a SHOULD in RFC 6125 and finally removed in RFC 9525. Browsers have not
supported this field since 2012.
records.heading: Common Name support in TLS certificates for OpenSSL

scheduled.sentence: In the release after 8.23.0 curl removes support for this field in code we control - which primarily means in the OpenSSL (and forks) backend.

records.section: Items to be removed from future curl releases
records.title: Common Name support in TLS certificates for OpenSSL

records.first-paragraph:
Some features and functionality in curl and libcurl are considered
**EXPERIMENTAL**.
records.title: Experimental

records.first-paragraph:
1. Each experimental feature should have a set of documented requirements of
   what is needed for that feature to graduate. Graduation means being removed
   from the list of experiments.
2. An experiment should NOT graduate if it needs test cases to be disabled,
   unless they are for minor features that are clearly documented as not
   provided by the experiment and then the disabling should be managed inside
   each affected test case.
records.heading: Graduation
records.title: Graduation

records.first-paragraph: Graduation requirements:
graduation-requirements: The library should be considered out-of-beta
a reasonable expectation of a stable API going forward
HTTP/3 with the given build should perform without risking busy-loops
records.heading: The quiche QUIC and HTTP/3 backend
records.title: The quiche QUIC and HTTP/3 backend

records.first-paragraph:
Support for HTTP/3 proxy and CONNECT-UDP tunneling is experimental and
requires an explicit build-time opt-in (`--enable-proxy-http3` for
autotools, `-DUSE_PROXY_HTTP3=ON` for CMake).
graduation-requirements: implementation stability over time with no known severe regressions
records.heading: HTTP/3 proxy and CONNECT-UDP support
records.title: HTTP/3 proxy and CONNECT-UDP support

records.first-paragraph: Graduation requirements:
graduation-requirements: a reasonable expectation of a stable API going forward.
records.heading: The Rustls TLS backend
records.title: The Rustls TLS backend

records.first-paragraph:
Use of the HTTPS resource record and Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) when using
DoH
graduation-requirements: ECH support exists in at least one widely used TLS library apart from BoringSSL and wolfSSL.
feedback from users saying that ECH works for their use cases
it has been given time to mature, so no earlier than April 2025 (twelve months after being added here)
records.heading: ECH
records.title: ECH

records.first-paragraph:
Import/Export of SSL sessions tickets in libcurl and curl command line
option '--ssl-session <filename>' for faster TLS handshakes and use
of TLSv1.3/QUIC Early Data (0-RTT).
graduation-requirements: the implementation is considered safe
feedback from users saying that session export works for their use cases
records.heading: SSL session import/export
records.title: SSL session import/export

records.first-paragraph:
HTTPS records support is a requirement for ECH but is provided as a
stand-alone feature that is itself considered EXPERIMENTAL.
graduation-requirements: HTTPS records work for DoH, c-ares and the threaded resolver
HTTPS records can control ALPN and port number, at least
There are options to control HTTPS use
records.heading: HTTPS RR
records.title: HTTPS RR

records.first-paragraph:
Sign outgoing HTTP requests according to RFC 9421 using the
`--httpsig-algo`, `--httpsig-key`, `--httpsig-keyid` and
`--httpsig-headers` command line options, or the corresponding
`CURLOPT_HTTPSIG_*` libcurl options. Built only when configured with
`--enable-httpsig`.
graduation-requirements: the option set (names, arguments, defaults) is settled
interoperability has been verified against at least two independent RFC 9421 implementations
no test cases are disabled for the feature
feedback from users saying the API works for their use cases
records.heading: HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421)
records.title: HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421)

records.first-paragraph:
There are undocumented system calls available in Apple operating systems that
when used allow for faster sending and receiving of UDP messages.
graduation-requirements: testimonials from users that these work reliably
measurements that show they make a measurable performance impact
an easy way to (re-)build curl to not use these functions
records.heading: Apple fast UDP
records.title: Apple fast UDP

records.first-paragraph:
These are problems and bugs known to exist at the time of this release. Feel
free to join in and help us correct one or more of these. Also be sure to
check the changelog of the current development status, as one or more of these
problems may have been fixed or changed somewhat since this was written.
records.title: Known bugs intro

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 10457](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/10457)
records.heading: IMAPS connection fails with Rustls error
records.title: IMAPS connection fails with Rustls error

records.first-paragraph:
When using Schannel to do client certs, curl sets `PKCS12_NO_PERSIST_KEY` to
avoid leaking the private key into the filesystem. Unfortunately that flag
instead seems to trigger a crash.
records.heading: Access violation sending client cert with Schannel
records.title: Access violation sending client cert with Schannel

records.first-paragraph: See [curl issue 3145](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3145)
records.heading: Client cert (MTLS) issues with Schannel
records.title: Client cert (MTLS) issues with Schannel

records.first-paragraph:
In old versions of Windows such as 7 and 8.1 the Schannel TLS 1.2 handshake
implementation likely has a bug that can rarely cause the key exchange to
fail, resulting in error SEC_E_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL or SEC_E_MESSAGE_ALTERED.
records.heading: Schannel TLS 1.2 handshake bug in old Windows versions
records.title: Schannel TLS 1.2 handshake bug in old Windows versions

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 15801](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/15801)
records.heading: mbedTLS and CURLE_AGAIN handling
records.title: mbedTLS and CURLE_AGAIN handling

records.first-paragraph: Certain Windows installations may be missing CA roots.
records.heading: Native CA roots incomplete on Windows with OpenSSL (or fork)
records.title: Native CA roots incomplete on Windows with OpenSSL (or fork)

records.heading: ECH not working through Proxy Tunnels
records.title: ECH not working through Proxy Tunnels

records.first-paragraph:
IMAP `SEARCH ALL` truncates output on large boxes. "A quick search of the code
reveals that `pingpong.c` contains some truncation code, at line 408, when it
deems the server response to be too large truncating it to 40 characters"
records.heading: IMAP `SEARCH ALL` truncated response
records.title: IMAP `SEARCH ALL` truncated response

records.first-paragraph:
The disconnect commands (`LOGOUT` and `QUIT`) may not be sent by IMAP, POP3
and SMTP if a failure occurs during the authentication phase of a connection.
records.heading: No disconnect command
records.title: No disconnect command

records.first-paragraph:
Specifying `--login-options AUTH=PLAIN` on the command line does not seem to
work correctly.
records.heading: `AUTH PLAIN` for SMTP is not working on all servers
records.title: `AUTH PLAIN` for SMTP is not working on all servers

records.first-paragraph: See [curl issue 10073](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/10073)
records.heading: `APOP` authentication fails on POP3
records.title: `APOP` authentication fails on POP3

records.heading: POP3 issue when reading small chunks
records.title: POP3 issue when reading small chunks

records.first-paragraph:
`-T` stats the path to figure out its size in bytes to use it as
`Content-Length` if it is a regular file.
records.heading: `-T /dev/stdin` may upload with an incorrect content length
records.title: `-T /dev/stdin` may upload with an incorrect content length

records.first-paragraph:
When the `<` shell operator is used. curl should realize that stdin is a
regular file in this case, and that it can do a non-chunked upload, like it
would do if you used `-T` file.
records.heading: `-T -` always uploads chunked
records.title: `-T -` always uploads chunked

records.first-paragraph:
curl for OS400 requires `QADRT` to build, which provides ASCII wrappers for
libc/POSIX functions in the ILE, but IBM no longer supports or even offers
this library to download.
records.heading: OS400 port requires deprecated IBM library
records.title: OS400 port requires deprecated IBM library

records.first-paragraph:
Compiling latest curl on HP-UX and linking against a custom OpenSSL (which is
on the default loader/linker path), fails because the generated Makefile has
`LDFLAGS` passed on after `LIBS`.
records.heading: `LDFLAGS` passed too late making libs linked incorrectly
records.title: `LDFLAGS` passed too late making libs linked incorrectly

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 8839](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/8839)
records.heading: Cygwin: make install installs curl-config.1 twice
records.title: Cygwin: make install installs curl-config.1 twice

records.first-paragraph:
We run many CI builds for each commit and PR on GitHub, and especially a
number of the Windows builds are flaky. This means that we rarely get all CI
builds go green and complete without errors. This is unfortunate as it makes
us sometimes miss actual build problems and it is surprising to newcomers to
the project who (rightfully) do not expect this.
records.heading: flaky CI builds
records.title: flaky CI builds

records.first-paragraph:
curl on Windows cannot access long paths (paths longer than 260 characters).
As a workaround, the Windows path prefix `\\?\` which disables all path
interpretation may work to allow curl to access the path. For example:
`\\?\c:\longpath`.
records.heading: long paths are not fully supported on Windows
records.title: long paths are not fully supported on Windows

records.first-paragraph: Passing in a Unicode filename with -o:
records.heading: Unicode on Windows
records.title: Unicode on Windows

records.first-paragraph:
`--aws-sigv4` hashes only the in-memory POST fields when it computes the payload hash, so a request
whose body comes from anywhere else is signed as if it had no body at all: the signature is
computed over `SHA256("")` while a different body goes on the wire. This affects `-F`
(multipart/form-data) and `-T` (PUT upload) alike.
records.heading: `--aws-sigv4` signs an empty payload hash for bodies not held in memory
records.title: `--aws-sigv4` signs an empty payload hash for bodies not held in memory

records.first-paragraph: We do not support auth-int for Digest using PUT or POST
records.heading: Digest `auth-int` for PUT/POST
records.title: Digest `auth-int` for PUT/POST

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl ignores the `domain` directive in Digest authentication challenges
(`WWW-Authenticate:`). RFC 7616 defines it as a quoted, space-separated list
of URIs that define the protection space.
records.heading: Digest does not care for `domain`
records.title: Digest does not care for `domain`

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl fails to build with MIT Kerberos for Windows (`KfW`) due to its
library header files exporting symbols/macros that should be kept private to
the library.
records.heading: MIT Kerberos for Windows build
records.title: MIT Kerberos for Windows build

records.first-paragraph:
When connecting via a proxy using `--proxy-any`, a failure to establish an
authentication causes libcurl to abort trying other options if the failed
method has a higher preference than the alternatives. As an example,
`--proxy-any` against a proxy which advertise Negotiate and NTLM, but which
fails to set up Kerberos authentication does not proceed to try authentication
using NTLM.
records.heading: libcurl can fail to try alternatives with `--proxy-any`
records.title: libcurl can fail to try alternatives with `--proxy-any`

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 3267](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3267)
records.heading: Do not clear digest for single realm
records.title: Do not clear digest for single realm

records.first-paragraph:
Windows builds of curl that have SSPI enabled use the native Windows API calls
to create authentication strings. The call to `InitializeSecurityContext` fails
with `SEC_E_QOP_NOT_SUPPORTED` which causes curl to fail with
`CURLE_AUTH_ERROR`.
records.heading: SHA-256 digest not supported in Windows SSPI builds
records.title: SHA-256 digest not supported in Windows SSPI builds

records.first-paragraph:
When doing an operation over FTP that requires the `ACCT` command (but not when
logging in), the operation fails since libcurl does not detect this and thus
fails to issue the correct command: https://curl.se/bug/view.cgi?id=635
records.heading: FTP with ACCT
records.title: FTP with ACCT

records.first-paragraph:
FTPS is not widely used with the Schannel TLS backend and so there may be more
bugs compared to other TLS backends such as OpenSSL. In the past users have
reported hanging and failed connections. It is likely some changes to curl
since then fixed the issues. None of the reported issues can be reproduced any
longer.
records.heading: FTPS server compatibility on Windows with Schannel
records.title: FTPS server compatibility on Windows with Schannel

records.first-paragraph:
When libcurl sends `CURLOPT_POSTQUOTE` commands when connected to an SFTP
server using the multi interface, the commands are not being sent correctly
and instead the connection is canceled (the operation is considered done)
prematurely. There is a half-baked (busy-looping) patch provided in the bug
report but it cannot be accepted as-is. See
https://curl.se/bug/view.cgi?id=748
records.heading: SFTP does not do `CURLOPT_POSTQUOTE` correct
records.title: SFTP does not do `CURLOPT_POSTQUOTE` correct

records.first-paragraph:
On this servers, the curl fails to create directories on the remote server
even when the `CURLOPT_FTP_CREATE_MISSING_DIRS` option is set.
records.heading: Remote recursive folder creation with SFTP
records.title: Remote recursive folder creation with SFTP

records.first-paragraph:
In the `SSH_SFTP_INIT` state for libssh, the ssh session working mode is set
to blocking mode. If the network is suddenly disconnected during sftp
transmission, curl is stuck, even if curl is configured with a timeout.
records.heading: libssh blocking and infinite loop problem
records.title: libssh blocking and infinite loop problem

records.first-paragraph: Running SCP and SFTP tests on Cygwin makes this warning message appear.
records.heading: Cygwin: "WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!"
records.title: Cygwin: "WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!"

records.first-paragraph:
When you give the `--interface` option telling curl to use a specific
interface for its outgoing traffic in combination with an IPv6 address in the
URL that uses a link-local scope, curl might pick the wrong address from the
named interface and the subsequent transfer fails.
records.heading: `--interface` with link-scoped IPv6 address
records.title: `--interface` with link-scoped IPv6 address

records.first-paragraph:
Even if a user edits `/etc/gai.conf` to prefer IPv4, curl still prefers and
tries IPv6 addresses first.
records.heading: Does not acknowledge getaddrinfo sorting policy
records.title: Does not acknowledge getaddrinfo sorting policy

records.first-paragraph:
After a successful SSPI/GSS-API exchange, the function queries and logs the
authenticated username and reports the supported data-protection level, but
then immediately deletes the negotiated SSPI security context and frees the
credentials before returning. The negotiated context is not stored on the
connection and is therefore never used to protect later SOCKS5 traffic.
records.heading: SOCKS-SSPI discards the security context
records.title: SOCKS-SSPI discards the security context

records.first-paragraph:
curl supports using a Unix domain socket path for speaking SOCKS to a proxy,
by providing a filename in the URL used for `-x` (`CURLOPT_PROXY`), but that
path cannot be a proper absolute Windows path with a drive letter etc.
records.heading: cannot use absolute Unix domain filename for SOCKS on Windows
records.title: cannot use absolute Unix domain filename for SOCKS on Windows

records.first-paragraph: The struct needs to be expanded and code added to store this info.
records.heading: GSSAPI library name + version is missing in `curl_version_info()`
records.title: GSSAPI library name + version is missing in `curl_version_info()`

records.first-paragraph:
The `connection-monitor` feature of the HTTP test server does not work
properly if some tests are run in unexpected order. Like 1509 and then 1525.
records.heading: HTTP test server 'connection-monitor' problems
records.title: HTTP test server 'connection-monitor' problems

records.first-paragraph:
`CURLINFO_LOCAL_PORT` (and possibly a few other) fails when TCP Fast Open is
enabled.
records.heading: Connection information when using TCP Fast Open
records.title: Connection information when using TCP Fast Open

records.first-paragraph: Occasionally, one of the tests timeouts. Inexplicably.
records.heading: test cases sometimes timeout
records.title: test cases sometimes timeout

records.first-paragraph:
It is unclear if the same option should even cover the proxy connection or if
it requires a separate option.
records.heading: `CURLOPT_CONNECT_TO` does not work for HTTPS proxy
records.title: `CURLOPT_CONNECT_TO` does not work for HTTPS proxy

records.first-paragraph: Test 165 disabled when built with WinIDN.
records.heading: WinIDN test failures
records.title: WinIDN test failures

records.first-paragraph:
When curl has been built with specific features or protocols disabled, setting
such options with `curl_easy_setopt()` should rather return
`CURLE_NOT_BUILT_IN` instead of `CURLE_UNKNOWN_OPTION` to signal the
difference to the application
records.heading: setting a disabled option should return `CURLE_NOT_BUILT_IN`
records.title: setting a disabled option should return `CURLE_NOT_BUILT_IN`

records.first-paragraph:
By configuration defaults, OpenLDAP automatically chase referrals on secondary
socket descriptors. The OpenLDAP backend is asynchronous and thus should
monitor all socket descriptors involved. Currently, these secondary
descriptors are not monitored, causing OpenLDAP library to never receive data
from them.
records.heading: OpenLDAP hangs after returning results
records.title: OpenLDAP hangs after returning results

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 3116](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3116)
records.heading: LDAP on Windows does authentication wrong?
records.title: LDAP on Windows does authentication wrong?

A simple curl command line getting `ldap://ldap.forumsys.com` returns an error
that says `no memory` !
records.heading: LDAP on Windows does not work
records.title: LDAP on Windows does not work

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 9580](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/9580)
records.heading: LDAPS requests to Active Directory server hang
records.title: LDAPS requests to Active Directory server hang

records.first-paragraph:
It probably does not happen too easily because of how slow and infrequent
sends are normally performed.
records.heading: telnet code does not handle partial writes properly
records.title: telnet code does not handle partial writes properly

records.first-paragraph:
This makes `--local-port [range]` to not work since curl cannot properly
detect if a port is already in use, so it tries the first port, uses that and
then subsequently fails anyway if that was actually in use.
records.heading: Trying local ports fails on Windows
records.title: Trying local ports fails on Windows

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 12641](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/12641)
records.heading: HTTP/2 prior knowledge over proxy
records.title: HTTP/2 prior knowledge over proxy

records.first-paragraph:
If the server sends HTTP/2 frames (like for example an HTTP/2 PING frame) to
curl while the connection is held in curl's connection pool, the socket is
found readable when considered for reuse and that makes curl think it is dead
and then it is closed and a new connection gets created instead.
records.heading: HTTP/2 frames while in the connection pool kill reuse
records.title: HTTP/2 frames while in the connection pool kill reuse

records.first-paragraph:
Infinite retries with 2 parallel requests on one connection receiving `GOAWAY`
with `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` error code.
records.heading: `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` causes infinite retries
records.title: `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` causes infinite retries

records.first-paragraph:
It has been observed that by making the speed limit less accurate we could
improve this performance. (by reverting
[db5c9f4f9e0779](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/db5c9f4f9e0779b49624752b135281a0717b277b))
Can we find a golden middle ground?
records.heading: HTTP/2 + TLS spends a lot of time in recv
records.title: HTTP/2 + TLS spends a lot of time in recv

records.heading: connection migration does not work
records.title: connection migration does not work

records.first-paragraph: The transfer ends with error "QUIC connection is draining".
records.heading: quiche: QUIC connection is draining
records.title: quiche: QUIC connection is draining

records.first-paragraph:
This is an incomplete list of known risks when running and using curl and
libcurl.
records.title: Known Risks

records.first-paragraph:
When using curl to perform transfers with protocols that are insecure or the
server identity is unverified, everything that is sent and received can be
intercepted by eavesdroppers and the servers can easily be spoofed by
impostors.
records.heading: Insecure transfers
records.title: Insecure transfers

records.first-paragraph:
You should **never** run curl command lines or use curl config files provided
to you from untrusted sources.
records.heading: Untrusted input
records.title: Untrusted input

records.first-paragraph:
The command line tool and its options should be used and be expected to work
as documented. Relying on undocumented functions or side-effects is unreliable
as they may cause problems or get changed behavior between releases.
records.heading: Command line misuse
records.title: Command line misuse

records.first-paragraph:
Applications using the libcurl API in a way that is not documented to work or
even documented to not work, is unsafe and might cause security problems. We
only guarantee secure and proper functionality when the APIs are used as
documented.
records.heading: API misuse
records.title: API misuse

records.first-paragraph:
When there is a local attacker present locally, curl cannot prevent such an
adversary to use curl's full potential. Possibly in malicious ways.
records.heading: Local attackers already present
records.title: Local attackers already present

records.first-paragraph:
When there is a remote attacker already present in the server, curl cannot
protect its operations against mischief. For example, if an attacker manages
to insert a symlink in your remote upload directory the upload may cause
havoc. Maybe the attacker makes certain responses come back with unexpected
content.
records.heading: Remote attackers already present
records.title: Remote attackers already present

records.first-paragraph:
We encourage users to test curl experiments and use debug code, but only in
controlled environments and setups - never in production.
records.heading: Debug & Experiments
records.title: Debug & Experiments

records.first-paragraph:
URL parser inconsistencies between browsers and curl are expected and are not
considered security vulnerabilities. The WHATWG URL Specification and RFC
3986+ (the plus meaning that it is an extended version) [are not completely
interoperable](https://github.com/bagder/docs/blob/master/URL-interop.md).
records.heading: URL inconsistencies
records.title: URL inconsistencies

records.first-paragraph:
The curl command blanks the contents of a number of command line arguments to
prevent them from appearing in process listings. It does not blank all
arguments, even though some that are not blanked might contain sensitive data.
records.heading: Visible command line arguments
records.title: Visible command line arguments

records.first-paragraph:
It is powerful to provide a set of custom headers to curl. Beware that when
asking curl to follow HTTP redirects, it also sends those headers to the new
URL which might be a different server. That might do another redirect etc.
records.heading: HTTP headers in redirects
records.title: HTTP headers in redirects

records.first-paragraph:
When asked to provide verbose output and trace logging, curl may output and
show details that are private and sensitive. Like for example raw credentials
or the password weakly disguised using base64 encoding.
records.heading: Verbose logs
records.title: Verbose logs

records.first-paragraph:
Content that is transferred from a server and gets displayed in a terminal by
curl may contain escape sequences or use other tricks to fool the user. Escape
sequences, moving cursor, changing color etc, is also frequently used for
good. To reduce the risk of getting fooled, save files and browse them after
download using a display method that minimizes risks.
records.heading: Terminal output and escape sequences
records.title: Terminal output and escape sequences

records.first-paragraph:
Every curl build is made to use a range of third party libraries. Each third
party library also needs to be safe and secure for the entire operation to be
risk-free.
records.heading: Legacy dependencies
records.title: Legacy dependencies

records.first-paragraph:
curl supports several cryptographic algorithms that are considered weak, like
DES and MD5. These algorithms are still in use because some protocols and
transfer options require use of them. For example NTLM or legacy HTTP Digest
authentication.
records.heading: Weak algorithms
records.title: Weak algorithms

records.first-paragraph:
When asking curl or libcurl to automatically decompress data on arrival, there
is a risk that the size of the output from the decompression process ends up
many times larger than the input data size.
records.heading: Compression bombs
records.title: Compression bombs

records.first-paragraph:
Things to do in project curl. Please tell us what you think, contribute and
send us patches that improve things.
records.title: TODO intro

records.first-paragraph:
Use `struct lifreq` and `SIOCGLIFADDR` instead of `struct ifreq` and
`SIOCGIFADDR` on newer Solaris versions as they claim the latter is obsolete.
To support IPv6 interface addresses for network interfaces properly.
records.heading: `struct lifreq`
records.title: `struct lifreq`

records.first-paragraph:
The share interface could benefit from allowing the alt-svc cache to be
possible to share between easy handles.
records.heading: alt-svc sharing
records.title: alt-svc sharing

records.first-paragraph:
Using the share interface users can share some data between easy handles but
several of the sharing options are documented as not safe and supported to
share between multiple concurrent threads. Fixing this would enable more users
to share data in more powerful ways.
records.heading: thread-safe sharing
records.title: thread-safe sharing

records.first-paragraph:
If `/etc/resolv.conf` gets updated while a program using libcurl is running, it
may cause name resolves to fail unless `res_init()` is called. We should
consider calling `res_init()` + retry once unconditionally on all name resolve
failures to mitigate against this. Firefox works like that. Note that Windows
does not have `res_init()` or an alternative.
records.heading: updated DNS server while running
records.title: updated DNS server while running

records.first-paragraph:
curl creates most sockets via the CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION callback and
close them with the CURLOPT_CLOSESOCKETFUNCTION callback. c-ares does not use
those functions and instead opens and closes the sockets itself. This means
that when curl passes the c-ares socket to the CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION it is
not owned by the application like other sockets.
records.heading: c-ares and CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION
records.title: c-ares and CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl's connection cache or pool holds a number of open connections for the
purpose of possible subsequent connection reuse. It may contain a few up to a
significant amount of connections. Currently, libcurl leaves all connections
as they are and first when a connection is iterated over for matching or reuse
purpose it is verified that it is still alive.
records.heading: Monitor connections in the connection pool
records.title: Monitor connections in the connection pool

records.first-paragraph:
Given a URL that for example contains spaces, libcurl could have an option
that would try somewhat harder than it does now and convert spaces to %20 and
perhaps URL encoded byte values over 128 etc (do what the redirect following
code already does).
records.heading: Try to URL encode given URL
records.title: Try to URL encode given URL

records.first-paragraph:
IRIs (RFC 3987) allow localized, non-ASCII, names in the URL. To properly
support this, curl/libcurl would need to translate/encode the given input
from the input string encoding into percent encoded output "over the wire".
records.heading: Add support for IRIs
records.title: Add support for IRIs

records.first-paragraph:
Allow an application to specify a list of proxies to try, and failing to
connect to the first go on and try the next instead until the list is
exhausted. Browsers support this feature at least when they specify proxies
using `PAC`.
records.heading: try next proxy if one does not work
records.title: try next proxy if one does not work

records.first-paragraph:
curl and libcurl provide timing information via a set of different time-stamps
(CURLINFO_*_TIME). When curl is following redirects, those returned time value
are the accumulated sums. An improvement could be to offer separate timings
for each redirect.
records.heading: provide timing info for each redirect
records.title: provide timing info for each redirect

records.first-paragraph:
Return information about the transfer's current pause state, in both
directions. See [curl issue 2588](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/2588)
records.heading: CURLINFO_PAUSE_STATE
records.title: CURLINFO_PAUSE_STATE

records.first-paragraph:
When libcurl fails to connect to a host, it could offer the application the
addresses that were used in the attempt. Source + destination IP, source +
destination port and protocol (UDP or TCP) for each failure. Possibly as a
callback. Perhaps also provide reason.
records.heading: Expose tried IP addresses that failed
records.title: Expose tried IP addresses that failed

records.first-paragraph:
Introducing a concept and system to erase secrets from memory after use, it
could help mitigate and lessen the impact of (future) security problems etc.
However: most secrets are passed to libcurl as clear text from the application
and then clearing them within the library adds nothing...
records.heading: erase secrets from heap/stack after use
records.title: erase secrets from heap/stack after use

records.first-paragraph:
Some options are not inherited because they are not relevant for the DoH SSL
connections, or inheriting the option may result in unexpected behavior. For
example the user's debug function callback is not inherited because it would
be unexpected for internal handles (i.e DoH handles) to be passed to that
callback.
records.heading: make DoH inherit more transfer properties
records.title: make DoH inherit more transfer properties

records.first-paragraph:
Make sure we do not ever loop because of non-blocking sockets returning
`EWOULDBLOCK` or similar. Blocking cases include:
records.heading: More non-blocking
records.title: More non-blocking

records.first-paragraph:
If a name resolve has been initiated for a given name and a second easy handle
wants to resolve that same name as well, make it wait for the first resolve to
end up in the cache instead of doing a second separate resolve. This is
especially needed when adding many simultaneous handles using the same
hostname when the DNS resolver can get flooded.
records.heading: Better support for same name resolves
records.title: Better support for same name resolves

records.first-paragraph:
The multi interface has a few API calls that assume a blocking behavior, like
`add_handle()` and `remove_handle()` which limits what we can do internally.
The multi API need to be moved even more into a single function that "drives"
everything in a non-blocking manner and signals when something is done. A
remove or add would then only ask for the action to get started and then
`multi_perform()` etc still be called until the add/remove is completed.
records.heading: Non-blocking `curl_multi_remove_handle()`
records.title: Non-blocking `curl_multi_remove_handle()`

records.first-paragraph:
The multi interface treats the authentication process as part of the connect
phase. As such any failures during authentication does not trigger the
relevant QUIT or LOGOFF for protocols such as IMAP, POP3 and SMTP.
records.heading: Split connect and authentication process
records.title: Split connect and authentication process

records.first-paragraph:
The multi_socket API should work with edge-triggered socket events. One of the
internal actions that need to be improved for this to work perfectly is the
`maxloops` handling in `transfer.c:readwrite_data()`.
records.heading: Edge-triggered sockets should work
records.title: Edge-triggered sockets should work

records.first-paragraph:
In libcurl 7.62.0 we introduced `curl_easy_upkeep`. It unfortunately only
works on easy handles. We should introduces a version of that for the multi
handle, and also consider doing `upkeep` automatically on connections in the
connection pool when the multi handle is in used.
records.heading: multi upkeep
records.title: multi upkeep

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl performs operations on the given file descriptor that presumes it is a
socket and an application cannot replace them at the moment. Allowing an
application to fully replace those would allow a larger degree of freedom and
flexibility.
records.heading: Virtual external sockets
records.title: Virtual external sockets

records.first-paragraph:
For users who do not use `curl_multi_wait()` or do not care for
`curl_multi_wakeup()`, we could introduce a way to make libcurl NOT create a
socketpair in the multi handle.
records.heading: dynamically decide to use socketpair
records.title: dynamically decide to use socketpair

records.first-paragraph: See [curl issue 6968](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/6968)
records.heading: Improve documentation about fork safety
records.title: Improve documentation about fork safety

records.first-paragraph:
Since listing the contents of a remove directory with FTP is returning the
list in a format and style the server likes without any established or even
defacto standard existing, it would be a feature to users if curl could parse
the directory listing and output a general curl format that is fixed and the
same, independent of the server's choice. This would allow users to better and
more reliably extract information about remote content via FTP directory
listings.
records.heading: A fixed directory listing format
records.title: A fixed directory listing format

records.first-paragraph:
In addition to currently supporting the SASL GSSAPI mechanism (Kerberos V5)
via third-party GSS-API libraries, such as MIT Kerberos, also add support for
GSSAPI authentication via Windows SSPI.
records.heading: GSSAPI via Windows SSPI
records.title: GSSAPI via Windows SSPI

records.first-paragraph:
Some FTP servers allow STAT for listing directories instead of using LIST, and
the response is then sent over the control connection instead of as the
otherwise used data connection.
records.heading: STAT for LIST without data connection
records.title: STAT for LIST without data connection

records.first-paragraph:
When doing FTP operations through a proxy at localhost, the reporter spotted
that curl only tried to connect once to the proxy, while it had multiple
addresses and a failed connect on one address should make it try the next.
records.heading: Passive transfer could try other IP addresses
records.title: Passive transfer could try other IP addresses

records.first-paragraph:
When curl receives a body response from a CONNECT request to a proxy, it
always reads and ignores it. It would make some users happy if curl instead
optionally would be able to make that response available. Via a new callback?
Through some other means?
records.heading: Provide the error body from a CONNECT response
records.title: Provide the error body from a CONNECT response

records.first-paragraph:
The `Retry-After` response header is said to dictate "the minimum time that
the user agent is asked to wait before issuing the redirected request" and
libcurl does not obey this.
records.heading: Obey `Retry-After` in redirects
records.title: Obey `Retry-After` in redirects

records.first-paragraph:
Server implementers often make an effort to detect browser and to reject
clients it can detect to not match. One of the last details we cannot yet
control in libcurl's HTTP requests, which also can be exploited to detect that
libcurl is in fact used even when it tries to impersonate a browser, is the
order of the request headers. I propose that we introduce a new option in
which you give headers a value, and then when the HTTP request is built it
sorts the headers based on that number. We could then have internally created
headers use a default value so only headers that need to be moved have to be
specified.
records.heading: Rearrange request header order
records.title: Rearrange request header order

records.first-paragraph:
curl only allows HTTP/2 push promise if the provided :authority header value
exactly matches the hostname given in the URL. It could be extended to allow
any name that would match the Subject Alternative Names in the server's TLS
certificate.
records.heading: Allow SAN names in HTTP/2 server push
records.title: Allow SAN names in HTTP/2 server push

records.first-paragraph:
Add the ability to specify the preferred authentication mechanism to use by
using `;auth=<mech>` in the login part of the URL.
records.heading: `auth=` in URLs
records.title: `auth=` in URLs

records.first-paragraph:
curl and libcurl provide options for trying higher HTTP versions (for example
HTTP/2) but then still allows the server to pick version 1.1. We could
consider adding a way to require a minimum version.
records.heading: Require HTTP version X or higher
records.title: Require HTTP version X or higher

records.first-paragraph:
Reading input (to send to the remote server) on stdin is a crappy solution for
library purposes. We need to invent a good way for the application to be able
to provide the data to send.
records.heading: ditch stdin
records.title: ditch stdin

records.first-paragraph:
Move the telnet support's network `select()` loop go away and merge the code
into the main transfer loop. Until this is done, the multi interface does not
work for telnet.
records.heading: ditch telnet-specific select
records.title: ditch telnet-specific select

records.first-paragraph: Add telnet feature negotiation data to the debug callback as header data.
records.heading: feature negotiation debug data
records.title: feature negotiation debug data

records.first-paragraph:
If it did, curl could be used to probe if there is an server there listening
on a specific port. That is, the following command would exit immediately
after the connection is established with exit code 0:
records.heading: exit immediately upon connection if stdin is /dev/null
records.title: exit immediately upon connection if stdin is /dev/null

records.first-paragraph:
Is there a way to pass the NOTIFY option to the CURLOPT_MAIL_RCPT option ? I
set a string that already contains a bracket. For instance something like
that: `curl_slist_append(recipients, "<foo@bar> NOTIFY=SUCCESS,FAILURE");`.
records.heading: Pass NOTIFY option to CURLOPT_MAIL_RCPT
records.title: Pass NOTIFY option to CURLOPT_MAIL_RCPT

records.first-paragraph:
Add the ability, for an application that uses libcurl, to obtain the list of
capabilities returned from the EHLO command.
records.heading: Enhanced capability support
records.title: Enhanced capability support

records.first-paragraph:
Rather than use the URL to specify the mail client string to present in the
`HELO` and `EHLO` commands, libcurl should support a new `CURLOPT`
specifically for specifying this data as the URL is non-standard and to be
honest a bit of a hack.
records.heading: Add `CURLOPT_MAIL_CLIENT` option
records.title: Add `CURLOPT_MAIL_CLIENT` option

records.first-paragraph:
Add the ability, for an application that uses libcurl, to obtain the list of
capabilities returned from the CAPA command.
records.heading: Enhanced capability support
records.title: Enhanced capability support

records.first-paragraph:
Add the ability, for an application that uses libcurl, to obtain the list of
capabilities returned from the CAPABILITY command.
records.heading: Enhanced capability support
records.title: Enhanced capability support

records.first-paragraph:
Currently the LDAP module only supports `ldap_simple_bind_s()` in order to
bind to an LDAP server. This function sends username and password details
using the simple authentication mechanism (as clear text). It should be
possible to use `ldap_bind_s()` instead specifying the security context
information ourselves.
records.heading: SASL based authentication mechanisms
records.title: SASL based authentication mechanisms

records.first-paragraph:
`CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` works perfectly for HTTPS and email protocols, but
it has no effect for LDAPS connections.
records.heading: `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` for LDAPS
records.title: `CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` for LDAPS

records.first-paragraph: [curl issue 4452](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/4452)
records.heading: Paged searches on LDAP server
records.title: Paged searches on LDAP server

records.first-paragraph: LDAPS not possible with macOS and Windows with Certificate-Based Authentication
records.heading: Certificate-Based Authentication
records.title: Certificate-Based Authentication

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl defaults to using binary WebSocket frames, which makes some servers
not work as they require text. We should make it possible to tell the tool to
use text frames.
records.heading: Support text frames with command line tool
records.title: Support text frames with command line tool

records.first-paragraph:
Transport Layer Security pre-shared key cipher suites (`TLS-PSK`) is a set of
cryptographic protocols that provide secure communication based on pre-shared
keys (`PSK`). These pre-shared keys are symmetric keys shared in advance among
the communicating parties.
records.heading: `TLS-PSK` with OpenSSL
records.title: `TLS-PSK` with OpenSSL

records.first-paragraph:
By changing the order of TLS extensions provided in the TLS handshake, it is
sometimes possible to circumvent TLS fingerprinting by servers. The TLS
extension order is of course not the only way to fingerprint a client.
records.heading: Defeat TLS fingerprinting
records.title: Defeat TLS fingerprinting

records.first-paragraph:
The Schannel backend does a lot of custom memory management we would rather
avoid: the repeated allocation + free in sends and the custom memory + realloc
system for encrypted and decrypted data. That should be avoided and reduced
for 1) efficiency and 2) safety.
records.heading: Less memory massaging with Schannel
records.title: Less memory massaging with Schannel

records.first-paragraph:
[DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities
(DANE)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6698) is a way to provide
SSL keys and certs over DNS using DNSSEC as an alternative to the CA model.
records.heading: Support DANE
records.title: Support DANE

records.first-paragraph:
TLS (1.3) offers optional record padding and OpenSSL provides an API for it. I
could make sense for libcurl to offer this ability to applications to make
traffic patterns harder to figure out by network traffic observers.
records.heading: TLS record padding
records.title: TLS record padding

records.first-paragraph:
AIA can provide various things like certificate revocation lists but more
importantly information about intermediate CA certificates that can allow
validation path to be fulfilled when the HTTPS server does not itself provide
them.
records.heading: Support Authority Information Access certificate extension (AIA)
records.title: Support Authority Information Access certificate extension (AIA)

records.first-paragraph:
Some TLS related options to the command line tool and libcurl are only
provided for the server and not for HTTPS proxies. `--proxy-tls-max`,
`--proxy-tlsv1.3`, `--proxy-curves` and a few more. For more Documentation on
this see: https://curl.se/libcurl/c/tls-options.html
records.heading: Some TLS options are not offered for HTTPS proxies
records.title: Some TLS options are not offered for HTTPS proxies

records.first-paragraph:
RFC 8740 explains how using HTTP/2 must forbid the use of TLS 1.3
post-handshake authentication. We should make sure to live up to that.
records.heading: Make sure we forbid TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication
records.title: Make sure we forbid TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication

records.first-paragraph:
Certain stupid networks and middle boxes have a problem with SSL handshake
packets that are within a certain size range because how that sets some bits
that previously (in older TLS version) were not set. The `clienthello`
extension adds padding to avoid that size range.
records.heading: Support the `clienthello` extension
records.title: Support the `clienthello` extension

records.first-paragraph:
For TLS backends that supports CA caching, it makes sense to allow the share
object to be used to store the CA cache as well via the share API. Would allow
multiple easy handles to reuse the CA cache and save themselves from a lot of
extra processing overhead.
records.heading: Share the CA cache
records.title: Share the CA cache

records.first-paragraph:
The feature matrix at https://curl.se/libcurl/c/tls-options.html shows which
features are supported by which TLS backends, and thus also where there are
feature gaps.
records.heading: Add missing features to TLS backends
records.title: Add missing features to TLS backends

records.first-paragraph: curl's support for ECH is currently limited to TCP only.
records.heading: ECH for QUIC
records.title: ECH for QUIC

records.first-paragraph:
When curl resolves a hostname, it might get a mix of IPv6 and IPv4 returned.
curl might then use an IPv6 address with a SOCKS5 proxy, which - if it does
not support IPv6 - returns "Address type not supported" and curl exits with
that error.
records.heading: Retry SOCKS handshake on address type not supported
records.title: Retry SOCKS handshake on address type not supported

records.first-paragraph:
The existing support for the `-E`/`--cert` and `--key` options could be
extended by supplying a custom certificate and key in PEM format, see:
[Getting a Certificate for
Schannel](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthn/getting-a-certificate-for-schannel)
records.heading: Extend support for client certificate authentication
records.title: Extend support for client certificate authentication

records.first-paragraph:
The existing support for the `--ciphers` option could be extended by mapping
the OpenSSL/GnuTLS cipher suites to the Schannel APIs, see [Specifying
Schannel Ciphers and Cipher
Strengths](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthn/specifying-schannel-ciphers-and-cipher-strengths).
records.heading: Extend support for the `--ciphers` option
records.title: Extend support for the `--ciphers` option

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl with Schannel errors without a known termination point from the server
(such as length of transfer, or SSL "close notify" alert) to prevent against a
truncation attack. Really old servers may neglect to send any termination
point. An option could be added to ignore such abrupt closures.
records.heading: Add option to allow abrupt server closure
records.title: Add option to allow abrupt server closure

records.first-paragraph:
Add support for other authentication mechanisms such as `OLP`, `GSS-SPNEGO`
and others.
records.heading: Other authentication mechanisms
records.title: Other authentication mechanisms

records.first-paragraph:
Currently the GSSAPI authentication only supports the default `QOP` of auth
(Authentication), whilst Kerberos V5 supports both `auth-int` (Authentication
with integrity protection) and `auth-conf` (Authentication with integrity and
privacy protection).
records.heading: Add `QOP` support to GSSAPI authentication
records.title: Add `QOP` support to GSSAPI authentication

records.first-paragraph:
SSH is a perfectly fine multiplexed protocols which would allow libcurl to do
multiple parallel transfers from the same host using the same connection, much
in the same spirit as HTTP/2 does. libcurl however does not take advantage of
that ability but does instead always create a new connection for new transfers
even if an existing connection already exists to the host.
records.heading: Multiplexing
records.title: Multiplexing

records.first-paragraph:
The SFTP code in libcurl checks the file size *before* a transfer starts and
then proceeds to transfer exactly that amount of data. If the remote file
grows while the transfer is in progress libcurl does not notice and does not
adapt. The OpenSSH SFTP command line tool does and libcurl could also attempt
to download more to see if there is more to get...
records.heading: Handle growing SFTP files
records.title: Handle growing SFTP files

records.first-paragraph:
The libssh2 backend in curl is limited to only reading keys from `id_rsa` and
`id_dsa`, which makes it fail connecting to servers that use more modern key
types.
records.heading: Read keys from `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519`
records.title: Read keys from `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519`

records.first-paragraph:
The two other `QUOTE` options are supported for SFTP, but this was left out
for unknown reasons.
records.heading: Support `CURLOPT_PREQUOTE`
records.title: Support `CURLOPT_PREQUOTE`

records.first-paragraph:
The SSH based protocols SFTP and SCP did not work over HTTPS proxy at all
until [curl pull request 6021](https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/6021) brought
the functionality with the libssh2 backend. Presumably, this support can/could
be added for the libssh backend as well.
records.heading: SSH over HTTPS proxy for libssh
records.title: SSH over HTTPS proxy for libssh

records.first-paragraph:
OpenSSH 9 switched their `scp` tool to speak SFTP under the hood. Going
forward it might be worth having curl or libcurl attempt SFTP if SCP fails to
follow suite.
records.heading: SFTP with `scp://`
records.title: SFTP with `scp://`

records.first-paragraph:
When asked to do transfers in parallel, the curl tool could be extended to use
a number of independent worker threads. This would allow faster transfers in
situations where curl becomes CPU bound.
records.heading: multi-threading
records.title: multi-threading

records.first-paragraph:
`curl --sync http://example.com/feed[1-100].rss` or
`curl --sync http://example.net/{index,calendar,history}.html`
records.heading: sync
records.title: sync

records.first-paragraph:
Globbing support for `-d` and `-F`, as in `curl -d "name=foo[0-9]" URL`. This
is easily scripted though.
records.heading: glob posts
records.title: glob posts

records.first-paragraph:
Allow the user to make curl run a command and use its stdio to make requests
and not do any network connection by itself. Example:
records.heading: `--proxycommand`
records.title: `--proxycommand`

records.first-paragraph:
RFC 6266 documents how UTF-8 names can be passed to a client in the
`Content-Disposition` header, and curl does not support this.
records.heading: UTF-8 filenames in Content-Disposition
records.title: UTF-8 filenames in Content-Disposition

records.first-paragraph:
When a user requests multiple line-based files using `-Z` and sends them to
stdout, curl does not *merge* and send complete lines but may send
partial lines from several sources.
records.heading: Option to make `-Z` merge line-based outputs on stdout
records.title: Option to make `-Z` merge line-based outputs on stdout

records.first-paragraph:
Allows a user to better specify exactly which error code(s) that are fine and
which are errors for their specific uses cases
records.heading: specify which response codes that make `-f`/`--fail` return error
records.title: specify which response codes that make `-f`/`--fail` return error

records.first-paragraph:
When using braces to download a list of URLs and you use complicated names
in the list of alternatives, it could be handy to allow curl to use other
names when saving.
records.heading: Choose the name of file in braces for complex URLs
records.title: Choose the name of file in braces for complex URLs

records.first-paragraph:
If you pull the scroll bar when transferring with curl in a Windows console
window, the transfer is interrupted and can get disconnected. This can
probably be improved. See [curl issue 322](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/322)
records.heading: improve how curl works in a Windows console window
records.title: improve how curl works in a Windows console window

records.first-paragraph:
The archive bit (`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE, 0x20`) separates files that shall be
backed up from those that are either not ready or have not changed.
records.heading: Windows: set attribute 'archive' for completed downloads
records.title: Windows: set attribute 'archive' for completed downloads

records.first-paragraph:
Provide an option that makes curl not exit after the last URL (or even work
without a given URL), and then make it read instructions passed on a pipe or
over a socket to make further instructions so that a second subsequent curl
invoke can talk to the still running instance and ask for transfers to get
done, and thus maintain its connection pool, DNS cache and more.
records.heading: keep running, read instructions from pipe/socket
records.title: keep running, read instructions from pipe/socket

records.first-paragraph:
Consider a command line option that can make curl do multiple serial requests
while acknowledging server specified [rate
limits](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/).
records.heading: Acknowledge `Ratelimit` headers
records.title: Acknowledge `Ratelimit` headers

records.first-paragraph:
A command line option that makes curl show exactly what it would do and send
if it would run for real.
records.heading: `--dry-run`
records.title: `--dry-run`

records.first-paragraph:
When `--retry` is used and curl actually retries transfer, it should use the
already transferred data and do a resumed transfer for the rest (when
possible) so that it does not have to transfer the same data again that was
already transferred before the retry.
records.heading: `--retry` should resume
records.title: `--retry` should resume

records.first-paragraph:
The `--retry` option retries transfers on *transient failures*. We later added
`--retry-connrefused` to also retry for *connection refused* errors.
records.heading: retry on network is unreachable
records.title: retry on network is unreachable

records.first-paragraph:
config files would be more powerful if they could set different configurations
depending on used URLs, hostname or possibly origin. Then a default `.curlrc`
could a specific user-agent only when doing requests against a certain site.
records.heading: hostname sections in config files
records.title: hostname sections in config files

records.first-paragraph:
When curl is told to `--retry` a failed transfer and follows redirects, it
might get an HTTP 429 response from the redirected-to URL and not the original
one, which then could make curl decide to rather retry the transfer on that
URL only instead of the original operation to the original URL.
records.heading: retry on the redirected-to URL
records.title: retry on the redirected-to URL

records.first-paragraph:
For SFTP and possibly FTP, curl could offer an option to set the modification
time for the uploaded file.
records.heading: Set the modification date on an uploaded file
records.title: Set the modification date on an uploaded file

records.first-paragraph:
To enhance transfer speed, downloading a single URL can be split up into
multiple separate range downloads that get combined into a single final
result.
records.heading: Use multiple parallel transfers for a single download
records.title: Use multiple parallel transfers for a single download

records.first-paragraph:
curl could offer an option to make escape sequence either non-functional or
avoid cursor moves or similar to reduce the risk of a user getting tricked by
clever tricks.
records.heading: Prevent terminal injection when writing to terminal
records.title: Prevent terminal injection when writing to terminal

records.first-paragraph:
`-J`/`--remote-header-name` does not decode %-encoded filenames. RFC 6266
details how it should be done. The can of worm is that we have no charset
handling in curl and ASCII >=128 is a challenge for us. Not to mention that
decoding also means that we need to check for nastiness that is attempted,
like `../` sequences and the like. Probably everything to the left of any
embedded slashes should be cut off. See https://curl.se/bug/view.cgi?id=1294

records.first-paragraph:
When using `-J` (with `-O`), automatically resumed downloading together with
`-C -` fails. Without `-J` the same command line works. This happens because
the resume logic is worked out before the target filename (and thus its
pre-transfer size) has been figured out. This can be improved.
records.heading: `-J` with `-C -`
records.title: `-J` with `-C -`

records.first-paragraph:
If using `--retry` and the transfer timeouts (possibly due to using -m or
`-y`/`-Y`) the next attempt does not resume the transfer properly from what
was downloaded in the previous attempt but truncates and restarts at the
original position where it was at before the previous failed attempt. See
https://curl.se/mail/lib-2008-01/0080.html
records.heading: `--retry` and transfer timeouts
records.title: `--retry` and transfer timeouts

records.first-paragraph:
Especially when having programs that execute curl via the command line, `PIE`
renders the exploitation of memory corruption vulnerabilities a lot more
difficult. This can be attributed to the additional information leaks being
required to conduct a successful attack. `RELRO`, on the other hand, masks
different binary sections like the `GOT` as read-only and thus kills a handful
of techniques that come in handy when attackers are able to arbitrarily
overwrite memory. A few tests showed that enabling these features had close to
no impact, neither on the performance nor on the general functionality of
curl.
records.heading: Enable `PIE` and `RELRO` by default
records.title: Enable `PIE` and `RELRO` by default

records.first-paragraph:
When compiling curl on OpenBSD with `--enable-debug` it gives linking errors
when you use GNU libtool. This can be fixed by using the libtool provided by
OpenBSD itself. However for this the user always needs to invoke make with
`LIBTOOL=/usr/bin/libtool`. It would be nice if the script could have some
logic to detect if this system is an OpenBSD host and then use the OpenBSD
libtool instead.
records.heading: Do not use GNU libtool on OpenBSD
records.title: Do not use GNU libtool on OpenBSD

records.first-paragraph:
libcurl unnecessarily allocates heap memory to hold the entire payload to get
sent, when the data is already perfectly accessible where it is when
`CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` is used. This is highly inefficient for larger payloads.
Additionally, libcurl does not support using the read callback for sending
MQTT which is yet another way to avoid having to hold large payload in memory.

does not support extracting that mode from the URL nor does it treat such
transfers specifically. It should probably do LF to CRLF translations for
them.
